title: Nike, Inc. — Consensus Investment Report
subtitle: A structured debate between five independent investment frameworks — Buffett owner-earnings value, Munger multidisciplinary quality, Damodaran fundamental valuation, Druckenmiller macro-first expectations, and Soros reflexivity — plus a standalone Minervini trading view, reconciled into a single synthesized analysis and recommendation.

exec_summary.lead: Nike is a genuinely great consumer brand — simple, durable-category, fortress balance sheet, #1 global share — whose moat is eroding and whose earnings power has roughly halved, trading at a 12-year low just above its 52-week low. Five frameworks split 3–2: the fundamental-quality majority (Buffett, Munger, Soros) sees **no margin of safety** at **$39.09** (base ~$34–40); Damodaran (B+) sees a cyclical trough mispriced as terminal (base $53.33) and would buy on weakness; Druckenmiller (B–) sees a 12–18-month tactical trade, not an investment; Minervini's trading view is F — do not buy. The consensus is **C — HOLD / WATCH**, do not initiate at ≥$39, and the entire debate turns on one question: is the decline a cycle (recoverable) or structural (permanent)?

profiles_lead: Each participant analyzed Nike independently. Their positions were then cross-examined in the debate. The Minervini lens is a standalone trading view and does not determine the consensus rating.

profiles.name: Warren Buffett
profiles.paragraph: Three-scenario 10%-hurdle DCF: bear ~$22, base ~$34, bull ~$47, weighted ~$33. At $39.09 the stock trades ~18% above my base value — **no margin of safety**. The brand, the fortress balance sheet, and the 24-year dividend record argue against avoid; the eroded moat and shrinking earnings power argue against buy. I become interested near **$23–28**; sell/reduce above ~$42.

profiles.name: Charlie Munger
profiles.paragraph: Conservative DCF (10.5% discount, 2% terminal growth): bear $28, base $38, bull $48, weighted ~$37.20. The **−49% FCF collapse** is a red flag on earnings quality — only 61 cents of cash per $1 of reported profit. A fair business at a fair price is not a good investment; two of eight avoid-stupidity checks fail. Accumulate **$29–33**, conviction **<$25**.

profiles.name: Aswath Damodaran
profiles.paragraph: Verified workbook (8.1% WACC, 2.5% terminal growth, margins normalizing toward ~12%): Severe Bear $2.39 / Bear $15.28 / Base **$53.33** / Bull $95.99 / Extreme Bull $162.58, weighted **$62.22** — **+59.2% upside**, **+9.7% 5-year annualized**. The market has conflated near-term cyclical weakness (China, wholesale) with structural decline. Buy zone **$30–45**, conviction **<$30**. Not a short.

profiles.name: Stanley Druckenmiller
profiles.paragraph: This is a 12–18-month mean-reversion trade, not a long-term hold. 12–18-month price expectations (not IV): bear $32–35, base $48–52, bull $62–70, weighted ~$46–48 — roughly **+20% expected 12-month return** with ~2:1 asymmetry. The market prices zero recovery; a modest one re-rates the stock violently given empty positioning and falling short interest. Buy **$38–42** tactical; sell rallies **$48–50**.

profiles.name: George Soros
profiles.paragraph: Mid-reflexive-bust near capitulation: the market's 'terminal decline' perception is an over-extrapolation, but the negative loop is unconfirmed-broken (JPM's FY28 headwinds). Weighted IV ~$40; 12-month expected return ≈ **+1%** at $39 with ~1.1x asymmetry — not a buy, not a short. Buy on dislocation **$28–33** or a confirmed inflection; the ~104% dividend payout is the tripwire.

profiles.name: Mark Minervini
profiles.role: SEPA / Trading View — NOT part of consensus rating
profiles.paragraph: Standalone trading view: **Stage 4** decline, **0/8** Trend Template, no pivot, severe RS laggard, no VCP — 'great company ≠ great trade.' Do not buy; watchlist only for a future Stage 1→2 base. Logical invalidation: a close below $38.86; first resistance $42.75 / $43.88 / $53.09; next earnings Sep 29, 2026 is a binary gap risk.

debate.title: The Debate: Agreement, Contention, Resolution
debate.lead: Round 1: opening statements. Round 2: uncontested common ground. Round 3: six disputed points, cross-examined to resolution. Round 4: final concessions — Damodaran concedes his B+ assumes the contested cycle view and accepts the ladder; Buffett concedes the brand and balance sheet argue against avoid; Munger concedes the bull case is real but refuses to pay for it; Druckenmiller concedes his B– is a trade with a defined exit; Soros concedes waiting is free; Minervini holds there is no technical entry today. Conclusion: a split 3–2 verdict resolved to C — HOLD/WATCH.
agreements: **This is a genuinely great consumer brand.** Simple, durable-category, asset-light; #1 global athletic share (~19%); premium pricing intact; 24-year dividend-growth record. The business quality is not in dispute.

**The moat is real but eroding — Moderate, not Wide.** Brand + scale + sports-marketing network effects remain; but consumer switching costs are minimal, On/Hoka/Brooks (~17% combined) and China locals are taking share, and UBS secondary-market prices are falling.

**The balance sheet is fortress-grade — no solvency or leverage reflexivity.** Net debt ≈ $2.0B (cash $9.0B vs debt $11.0B), interest coverage ~13–18×, Altman Z 4.31, current ratio 1.96. This caps the downside: no forced-selling loop.

**Earnings quality has deteriorated and the FCF collapse is real.** FCF $1.89B (−49% YoY), FCF/NI ~61%, OCF/NI <1, one-time $0.52/sh tariff benefit flattered Q4 EPS, $385M restructuring, SBC ~$715–800M/yr.
**The dividend is the fragile floor and the tripwire.** 4.03% fwd yield, ~104% forward payout on falling EPS, buybacks paused ($146M FY26) — sustainable only if EPS stops falling.

**China is the swing variable.** Greater China −11% FY26 to $5.85B; share −590 bps since 2019 to 12.9%; segment profit contribution down from 25% to 12%. China stabilization is the hinge between the cycle and structural narratives.

**Wholesale is recovering while Direct resets — a deliberate rebalancing, not pure demand destruction.** Wholesale +6% to $27.5B vs Direct −6% to $17.7B; the 'Win Now' store closures self-inflict near-term pain into FY28 (JPM).

**Nobody buys with long-term conviction at $39.09; nobody shorts.** Buffett/Munger/Soros: no margin of safety. Damodaran: buy on weakness, conviction below $30. Druckenmiller: a tactical trade, not an investment. Minervini: F — do not buy. The stock is too cheap, too oversold, and too short-covering to short reflexively.

**The one valuation-critical variable: China stabilization + margin recovery vs WACC.** Damodaran: 'if margins normalize toward 12% and China stabilizes, base is $53.33 — the market is pricing a structural bear.' Buffett/Munger/Soros: 'if the share loss is structural, base is $34–40 — the market is pricing fair value for a shrinking brand.'
debate.contentions_title: Contested points — and how they were resolved
contentions: **Reference price: intrinsic value today vs 12-month price path.** All five anchor on $39.09, but Buffett/Munger/Damodaran/Soros frame their cells as intrinsic value today while Druckenmiller frames his ($32–35 / $48–52 / $62–70) as 12–18-month price expectations. Druckenmiller concedes his cells are price paths, not IV. **Resolved:** the IV models set the consensus IV; Druckenmiller informs the near-term ladder and triggers (his cells carry a † in the matrix).

**Where does base-case intrinsic value sit?** Buffett ~$34 (10% hurdle, partial structural share loss), Munger $38 (10.5% / 2%), Soros ~$40 (reflexive), Druckenmiller $48–52 (12-mo price path, not IV), Damodaran **$53.33** (verified workbook — assumes margin normalization and China stabilization). Munger challenges Damodaran: 'you are capitalizing the recovery'; Damodaran counters: 'normalizing a cyclical trough is not optimism.' **Resolved:** consensus base ≈ **~$40** — the top of the fundamental cluster, partially crediting Damodaran's cycle case; his $53.33 becomes the 'cycle-recovery' upgrade target.

**How much credit for the right tail?** Damodaran bull $95.99 / extreme $162.58 (25% / 10%) vs Buffett ~$47, Munger ~$48, Soros ~$50–56, Druckenmiller $62–70 (aggressive). Damodaran's bull requires China to re-accelerate at +5% CAGR and DTC at 35–40% of revenue — the majority regards that as low-probability for a brand whose share is falling. Damodaran concedes his distribution is right-skewed: 'the median sits well below the weighted value.' **Resolved:** consensus bull ≈ **~$58**, extreme ≈ **~$85**; his cells stand but are not fully credited.

**What price compensates for the uncertainty?** Buffett $23–28; Munger $29–33 (conviction <$25); Damodaran $30–45 (conviction <$30); Druckenmiller $38–42 (tactical only); Soros $28–33 (dislocation). Damodaran: 'at $30–45 the expected return finally compensates; demanding $25 implies you believe the bear case is the base case.' Munger: 'I refuse to pay for the option; the margin of safety is the whole point.' **Resolved (unanimous):** composite ladder — watch $33–39, accumulate $28–33, high-conviction $23–28, exceptional <$23. The dispute is sizing and temperament; nobody buys with conviction at $39.

**Management quality — Elliott Hill turnaround credibility.** Buffett 7/10 (integrity, candor, insider buys at $42–43, historically strong allocation now strained); Munger 6/10 (defensive capital allocation, missed demand signals, inventory defense); Damodaran 'credible — turnaround in progress'; Druckenmiller ~70% high-confidence; Soros 'insiders bought above today's price but austerity self-inflicts pain and the CFO was replaced.' **Resolved:** consensus **6/10** — credible, candid, insider-aligned, but entirely unproven; JPM's FY28-headwinds call is live; the Q1 FY27 print (Sep 29, 2026) is the first hard test.

**Is the decline a cycle (recoverable) or structural (China/wholesale) — the single biggest disagreement.** Damodaran: cycle (China comps easing, margins normalize toward ~12% EBIT, DTC runway, World Cup); Druckenmiller: cycle-ish (China stabilizes by early 2027, trough FY27); Buffett/Munger/Soros: partly structural (China share −590 bps, ankle-biters at ~17%, moat moderate and eroding, FCF −49% as evidence demand is broken, not just timing). Damodaran concedes his case rests on the recovery showing up; Munger concedes wholesale +6% and the World Cup are real but refuses to pay for them; Soros concedes the market may be over-extrapolating, but the negative loop is unconfirmed-broken. **Resolved:** NOT cleanly resolved — the consensus prices ~40% of the cycle-recovery view into its base (~$40) and treats the question as the decisive, monitored uncertainty; the Q1 FY27 print (Sep 29, 2026) and China/margin data will adjudicate.

valuation.title: Consensus Valuation
valuation.lead: Reconciled scenario matrix. The **Damodaran column is the verified workbook (ALL_MATCH) — authoritative, verbatim**. Druckenmiller/Soros columns are 12–18-month price expectations (†), not intrinsic value; they inform the near-term ladder and triggers, not the consensus IV. The consensus IV row is the majority reconciliation — closer to the fundamental lenses (Buffett/Munger/Soros) than to Damodaran, because the cycle-recovery assumptions his base requires are the contested core of the debate.
valuation.footnote: * Buffett: base $34 is his 10%-hurdle DCF; his bull is $47 and he caps the extreme tail at his bull value. ** Munger: base $38, bull $48; tail cells capped at his bull. † Druckenmiller/Soros cells are 12–18-month **price expectations**, not intrinsic values; they inform the near-term ladder and triggers, not the consensus IV. Damodaran column = verified `NKE_Damodaran_Financial_Model.xlsx` (ALL_MATCH): Severe Bear $2.39 / Bear $15.28 / Base $53.33 / Bull $95.99 / Extreme Bull $162.58, weighted $62.22.

weighted.text: At $39.09 that is roughly **+17% expected upside** and **≈ +3% 5-year annualized** — positive but thin, with **no margin of safety** for a 10%+ return seeker. The consensus weighted value (~$46) sits between the fundamental lenses' weighted values (Buffett ~$33, Munger ~$37, Soros ~$40) and Damodaran's workbook weighted value ($62.22), because the majority only partially credits the cycle-recovery case his base requires. Confidence: **Low/Medium** — the cycle-vs-structural question is unresolved and the ~104% dividend payout is the tripwire. **Reverse-DCF check (uncontested):** the $39.09 price implies roughly a ~2.8% FCFF CAGR (vs Damodaran's ~4.5%), ~1.5% terminal growth (vs 2.5%), or a ~9.5% WACC (vs 8.1%) — the market prices a **no-recovery, structural-bear scenario**. It does not assume an impossible business; it prices one for zero success. Downside tail (severe bear) ≈ −38% from price; upside tail (extreme bull) ≈ +117%.

ladder.title: Consensus Price Ladder
ladder.lead: Where the six views meet. **Do-not-initiate band: $39 and above** — the current price ($39.09) sits inside it. The fundamental majority (Buffett, Munger, Soros) refuses to buy above ~$33; Damodaran's buy-on-weakness zone ($30–45) and Druckenmiller's tactical trade ($38–42) are the only constructive voices near the price, and neither is a long-term-conviction buy here.

conclusions.title: The Five Consensus Conclusions
items: **The Business.** Nike is a genuinely great consumer brand — simple, durable-category, asset-light, #1 global athletic share (~19%), premium pricing intact — but with a moat that is **real and eroding** (Moderate, not Wide): China share −590 bps since 2019, ankle-biters (On/Hoka/Brooks) at ~17% combined, falling secondary-market prices. The business quality is not in dispute; the trajectory is.

**The Economics.** The sole determinant of per-share value is whether the decline is a **cycle** — China stabilizes and margins normalize toward ~45.5% gross / 12% EBIT, unlocking Damodaran's $53.33 base — or **structural** — permanent share and margin loss, capping value at the $34–40 fundamental cluster. China stabilization and margin recovery vs the ~8–9% cost of capital is the one valuation-critical variable.

**The Market's Expectations.** At $39.09 the market prices a **no-recovery structural bear**: ~2.8% FCFF CAGR, ~1.5% terminal growth, ~9.5% WACC — China lost, margins permanently compressed, no re-rating ever. That is not an impossible business; it is a business priced for zero success — which is exactly why Damodaran sees value (+59% to his base) and why the fundamental majority still sees no margin of safety (their base is $34–40).

**The Valuation.** Consensus base intrinsic value **~$40/share**; probability-weighted **~$46/share**; severe bear ~$24, bull ~$58, extreme tail ~$85. Damodaran's verified workbook: **$2.39 / $15.28 / $53.33 / $95.99 / $162.58**, weighted **$62.22**. Confidence: **Low/Medium**. At $39.09 expected upside ≈ **+17%** (5-yr annualized ≈ +3%) — positive but thin, and **no margin of safety** for a 10%+ return seeker.

**The Investment Decision.** **C — HOLD / WATCH at $39.09; do not initiate at ≥$39.** Accumulate $28–33, buy with conviction $23–28, exceptional <$23 — provided the monitoring hierarchy (China > margin > FCF/share > mix > dividend) stays intact. **Not a short.** Upgrades require proof; the Q1 FY27 print (Sep 29, 2026), China comps, and margin trajectory deliver the verdict.

judgment.title: Final Consensus Judgment
judgment.paragraph: At a price of **$39.09**, the market is pricing Nike as a structurally broken, no-growth brand — no China recovery, permanently compressed margins, no re-rating. The five frameworks split **3–2**, and the split is honest and worth respecting: the fundamental-quality majority (Buffett, Munger, Soros) sees a wonderful business at fair-to-slightly-rich value with **no margin of safety** (base ~$34–40); Damodaran sees a cyclical trough mispriced as terminal (base $53.33, weighted $62.22, +59% to base) and would buy on weakness, conviction below $30; Druckenmiller sees a 12–18-month mean-reversion trade (not a long-term investment); Minervini's trading lens flatly says avoid (Stage 4, 0/8 Trend Template). The consensus resolves to a **C — HOLD / WATCH**: do not initiate at $39.09; accumulate from **$28–33**, buy with conviction at **$23–28** and below. The disagreement is real and centers on **one question — cycle or structural?** — which the market, not the debate, will answer at the Q1 FY27 print on **September 29, 2026** and in the China and margin data. The 4% dividend is the fragile floor: a cut without a capital plan is the one event that could complete the crash to $25–28 (and create the real reversal entry); a guide-beat that snaps the oversold, short-covering market is the one that could re-rate the stock violently. We agree on the asset and disagree on the price path; the correct response is to wait, watch, and buy only the prices that compensate for the uncertainty.

This document is an educational synthesis of estimates about estimates — it is **not investment advice**, and no valuation herein should be treated as a price prediction or a recommendation to trade. Nike's outcome distribution is wide and the cycle-vs-structural question is genuinely unresolved; treat every number on this page as a hypothesis, not a fact.
